points.description: States that steepest descent is used to update the weights/parameters of the network during the learning (training) phase.
States that its purpose is to navigate the cost function to find the parameters/weights for which the cost is minimum (minimises the cost function).
States that weights are updated in the direction of steepest descent, i.e. opposite to the gradient vector (negative gradient) of the cost function.
States a limitation: it can get stuck in local minima and/or may become unstable.
points.partial_credit: Only one of local minima or instability named correctly is sufficient for full marks; vague 'has problems' earns nothing.

rubric.notes: Each point needs an explicit, correct statement; vague wording such as 'it improves the network' earns nothing. Saying the update is along the gradient (not opposite) or in the wrong direction cancels P3. Award 2 marks only if all four elements are stated precisely, using terms like weights, cost function, gradient vector and local minima.
